post.description:
Read this parlay's legs off the live boxscore.

Open to anyone in the season, like the season pick sync: it reads a public feed and
writes only `live_*` columns, so there is nothing here one gambler can do to another's
pick. It never touches `result` — void, push and bozo are judgements, and a settled
result entered by hand must not be overwritten by a number scraped mid-game.

Pull every season pick in this season up to date with ESPN.

Open to anyone in the season. It rewrites results across everyone's picks at once,
including weeks entered by hand, but ESPN is the source of truth for all of them — so
there is nothing here one gambler can do to another's pick that the next press would
not do anyway. Slow by nature, one ESPN call per distinct player or team, so it stays
a deliberate action rather than something a screen triggers on load.

The only way the sweep runs: nothing else calls it. Weeks stay as they were until
somebody presses this, so a spell of ESPN being unreachable is recovered by pressing
it again rather than by waiting.

get.description:
Everything at once, open and resolved.

There will never be many, and the client splits them by tab and by age. Comments are
the expensive part and are left until a suggestion is opened.

put.description:
Resolve, retire, or put one back into the open list.

Deliberately not guarded by require_open: reopening is the whole point of being able
to change a status, and an admin who retires something by mistake needs a way back.

get.description: Readable whatever the status: a settled suggestion's votes are part of its record.

put.description:
Toggle one emoji on one pick.

Unlike a feedback vote there is no single row per gambler to overwrite: several
different emoji may stand at once, so this only ever adds or removes the one sent.

Returns the whole pick so the client patches one object and the chips on the card and
in the open drawer — the same array — move together.

get.description:
The thread, in full or from a cursor.

Readable whatever the parlay's state: a closed pick's argument is part of its record.

get.description:
Every player priced for the games on one date.

Served from a cache that refetches only once it is a quarter of an hour old, so five
people opening the same slate costs one call rather than five — which is what keeps the
monthly budget intact.

An empty players list is a real answer, not a failure: a date with no games, one too
far ahead to be priced, or a slate already played all look like this.

post.description:
Resolve missing ESPN ids across every player target, then correct their teams.

Slow in proportion to how many players the league has ever bet on, and worth running
after an offseason rather than on a timer: a badge that is a club out of date is the
symptom, and it only appears when somebody moves.

CorrectionSuggestion.title: CorrectionSuggestion
CorrectionSuggestion.description:
The model's proposal for one pick.

There is deliberately no field capable of expressing a target or prop-type
change: the "only the number moves" rule is enforced by this shape rather
than by prompt compliance.

ExtractedLeg.title: ExtractedLeg
ExtractedLeg.description:
A single bet leg read off an uploaded parlay screenshot.

`raw_text` is carried through to the review UI so a reviewer can see what the
model actually read, which is the only practical check on alternate-line
normalization (`2+` becoming Over 1.5).

FeedbackVotersResponseData.title: FeedbackVotersResponseData
FeedbackVotersResponseData.description:
Who voted, by first name.

Kept off the list response: it is a handful of names per suggestion and the cards show
only the total, so fetching them for every row to render none of them would be waste.

PickCommentResponseData.title: PickCommentResponseData
PickCommentResponseData.description: Field for field FeedbackCommentResponseData, on a different parent.

PickReactionResponseData.title: PickReactionResponseData
PickReactionResponseData.description:
Everyone who left one emoji on one pick.

The ids rather than a count, deliberately. The season context already has every
gambler by id, so the client derives the count, whether the reader is in it, and the
names for the drawer from this one field — which is why PickResponseData.from_model
needs no notion of who is asking, and why "who reacted" needs no second request.
A league is a handful of people; the list is smaller than a count plus a viewer flag.

ReactionRequestData.title: ReactionRequestData
ReactionRequestData.description: The emoji tapped. Sending one you already left takes it back.

ScoredMetrics.title: ScoredMetrics
ScoredMetrics.description:
The sample a season's rules actually score on.

Both the whole-season metrics and a single slate bucket carry these three fields,
so a corrector can return either and the client renders it without needing to know
which. Keeps the stats shown beside a score from disagreeing with it.

SeasonPickKind.title: SeasonPickKind
SeasonPickKind.description:
Season-long picks come in two shapes. Team win totals deliberately have no
PropBetType member, which is what keeps them out of the parlay pick picker.

SyncParlayProgressResponseData.title: SyncParlayProgressResponseData
SyncParlayProgressResponseData.description:
The refreshed parlay, plus what the sweep could and could not answer.

The whole parlay comes back rather than just the numbers: every leg's state and detail
may have moved, and re-reading them from one response is simpler than patching each.

SyncPlayersResponseData.title: SyncPlayersResponseData
SyncPlayersResponseData.description:
Enough to tell a sweep that worked from one that quietly matched nothing.

`ids_failed` names the players ESPN could not find, which is the list worth acting on:
a target with no athlete id is invisible to every later refresh until its name is
fixed.

SyncSeasonPicksResponseData.title: SyncSeasonPicksResponseData
SyncSeasonPicksResponseData.description:
What the sweep did, rather than a bare success.

A sync that quietly matched nothing looks identical to one that worked unless it says
how much it touched — and `skipped` names the picks ESPN could not answer for, which
is the list worth acting on.

TimeSeriesDatum.title: TimeSeriesDatum
TimeSeriesDatum.description:
One point on the score line.

Deliberately does not carry metrics. It used to embed a full GamblerBaseMetrics per
point, which meant a season shipped megabytes of per-target and per-prop breakdowns
to draw a line the client renders from corrected_score alone.

VoteRequestData.title: VoteRequestData
VoteRequestData.description: The direction tapped. Sending the same one again takes the vote back.

WeeksProgressRequestData.title: WeeksProgressRequestData
WeeksProgressRequestData.description:
Several weeks at once, so catching up a whole season is one request rather than
one per week — each of which would otherwise re-derive and re-send the progress.
